source: Bulut (2026) It's the Problem, Not the Path: Budget and Difficulty Confounds in LLM Reasoning Trajectories
finding: Closest LLM test of continue vs restart at matched total tokens. Continuing the model's own prefix beat restarting wherever the budget match was exact. Apparent breakthroughs were mostly budget artifacts, not a prefix that fresh compute could not replace.
numbers: 178 problem-model cells (89 MATH problems x 2 small models, 16,384-token traces). 1 of 178 cells prefix-limited; 98 cells collected after rules were frozen gave 0 new cases. Continuation beat restart 9 of 9 at exact match (2 more wins and 2 ties on proxies). A larger restart budget reached the same threshold in 11/13 and the prefix's own rate in 9/13. One model's unsolved problems went 0% to 79% with restart budget; the other stayed flat.
limits: Two small 4-bit open models (Gemma-4 E4B, Ministral-3 3B), MATH only, not insight items. A restart is not a break with a changed context. Single author, preprint.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: a restart or reset does not beat continuing at equal tokens in this test. Supports the schema leaving incubation out; a reset adds nothing a longer pass does not buy.

finding: Probes that seem to predict a run's fate early mostly read problem difficulty. Within a single problem they are at chance.
numbers: Trace-blind difficulty proxy AUROC 0.873 on 192K DeepSeek-R1 generations (published probe range 0.79 to 0.95). Matched reconstruction of the closest published probe: 0.849 pooled, 0.496 within problem at t=4 (chance at all ten anchors). Pre-registered single-shot test on held-out split (17 test problems): no gain beyond difficulty.
limits: Small models, MATH; the author does not claim hidden states never carry within-attempt information.
agent_relevance: Caution for our impasse detector (S6): any learned stuck-detector must be tested within problem, not pooled.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) The illusion of insight in reasoning models, Pass 2 tables and limits
finding: The second-pass (forced reconsideration) gain has no token-matched control in the paper. Pass 2 is a full extra generation. The intervention runs on small open models only.
numbers: Appendix table, math: Pass 1 32.70% to Pass 2 40.43% (+7.74pp, N = 464,000); high-entropy bucket 19.70% to 35.09% (+15.38pp); crosswords 9.65% to 10.15% (+0.49pp). Forced reconsideration on a MATH subset: Qwen2.5-7B +5.97pp, Llama 3.1-8B -4.19pp. A 1 SD rise in entropy multiplies the odds of correctness after the cue by about 2.2 to 2.5 across three cue wordings.
limits: Qwen2.5-1.5B, 7B, Llama 3.1-8B. No equal-token baseline; authors note compute cost and tested only a subset. Different tables give +8.41pp (main) and +7.74pp (appendix bucket table), so pick the table before quoting.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays open. Gain is plausibly extra compute, which d01 suggests a longer first pass could also buy. Gate any re-check step on uncertainty, not on a fixed cue phrase.

source: Yang, Wu, Chen, Xiao, Yang, Wong, Wang (2025) Understanding Aha Moments: from External Observations to Internal Mechanisms
finding: Aha is defined by comparing aha-trained and no-aha models and by anthropomorphic self-reflection wording. It is not defined by a change in the output. The paper reports reasoning collapse rates, not an accuracy effect size for aha.
numbers: Reasoning collapse (language mixing, token repetition, reasoning-path repetition) measured over 200 test samples per difficulty level. Aha models had mixing and path-repetition rates near zero at difficulty 3 to 6. Token repetition higher for aha models on easy items, lower above difficulty 5.
limits: Figures and silhouette scores; no confidence intervals or per-item accuracy effects found. Marker-based throughout.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: closes as 'no, not tested'. No output-change definition and no effect size. Treat Yang as showing style, not benefit.

source: Lin, Snell et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute, predictability section
finding: Predictability is measured as log-probability of the question given the context under Llama2-70B. Sleep-time gain over test-time compute widens as questions become more predictable. o1 shows limited gains.
numbers: Stateful GSM-Symbolic P1 and P2 binned into five predictability quantiles; accuracy gap widens from bin 1 to bin 5 (GPT-4o-mini). Up to +13% accuracy (GSM-Symbolic), +18% (AIME). SWE-Features case study: sleep-time helps at lower test-time budgets.
limits: Questions generated from context by design (predictable). No threshold value is given. Exact bin gap sizes read from a figure, not stated in text.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 partly closed: predictability matters, graded not thresholded. For an agent, pre-compute only where the next question is guessable.

source: IdleSpec (2026) Exploiting Idle Time via Speculative Planning for LLM Agents, arXiv 2605.22154, baselines table
finding: Sleep-time compute as a baseline gave no gain on tool-using agent benchmarks and hurt a small model. Authors blame hallucinated pre-generated context.
numbers: Average accuracy (GAIA levels plus FRAMES), vanilla / sleep-time / IdleSpec: Gemma4-E4B 30.9 / 31.0 / 35.5; Qwen3.5-4B 33.2 / 29.4 / 40.0; Gemini-2.5-Flash 50.5 / 50.1 / 55.6. MLE-Bench Lite gold rate 18.2% vanilla vs 13.6% sleep-time. FRAMES 50 samples; GAIA 165 tasks; 3 seeds.
limits: Authors' own method is the winner, so the baseline may be under-tuned. Small samples; the table was read from a garbled layout, row order inferred.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: in unpredictable tool-observation settings the return is zero or negative. Supports not adding idle-time pre-compute for open-ended tasks.

source: Du, Gordon and Tolmie (2025) incubation with 0-back task, Unusual Uses and Compound Remote Associates (Brain Sciences 15(6):595)
finding: Incubation gain was larger for repeated than novel items on Unusual Uses fluency but not on CRA. No no-incubation control group, so gains are baseline-to-post and confounded with a second try.
numbers: N = 85, within-subject. UUT fluency repeated t(84) = 9.53, d = 1.03; novel d = 0.47; repeated vs novel t(84) = 2.79, p = .006, d = 0.30. CRA repeated d = 0.37, novel d = 0.33, difference t(84) = 0.35, p = .72. Mind wandering about 0.13 to 0.16 of probes; no link to UUT gains.
limits: No control group; not true insight problems; one lab.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: the repeat-exposure dependence partly replicates on UUT, not on CRA, and no no-gap control exists. Mind wandering is not the driver.

source: Teng and Lien (2022) Propensity or diversity? Mind wandering and the incubation effect (PLoS One 17(4):e0267187)
finding: A Baird-style design with a no-task control did not show a mind-wandering benefit. Only a mindfulness break improved flexibility.
numbers: N = 90 (29 mind-wandering 0-back, 30 mindfulness, 31 control). Flexibility F(2,87) = 3.85, p = .025; mindfulness vs control d = 0.70 (p = .023); mind-wandering vs control p = 1.000. Fluency F = 1.55, p = .219; originality F = 1.51, p = .226. Repeated-item effect not tested.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: the claim that undemanding mind-wandering breaks beat other breaks is weak. Another reason not to model an idle step.

source: Beijamini, Valentin, Jager, Born and Diekelmann (2021) Sleep facilitates problem solving with no additional gain through targeted memory reactivation (Front Behav Neurosci 15:645110)
finding: Sleep helped solving a video-game insight challenge (about 10 h interval), but cueing during sleep added nothing. A different task from Sanders 2019.
numbers: Exp 1: N = 42 (21 sleep, 21 wake), 62% vs 24% solved. Exp 2: 81 volunteers, 23 excluded; solved 56% (SWS cue), 58% (REM cue), 57% (wake-period cue). More slow-wave sleep predicted solving in Exp 1.
limits: Different design: one problem, not many puzzles; not a direct replication of Sanders.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: cue-during-sleep does not replicate on another task. Resurfacing a cue is not shown to help; drop it as a design idea.

source: Follow-up to Sanders 2019 (2021) sleep, TMR and fixating information, J Cognitive Psychology, doi 10.1080/20445911.2021.1912050
finding: Per search summary only: cued puzzles solved numerically more than uncued, but only when puzzles had fixating information. Includes a Bayes factor against the original.
numbers: Numbers not read. Page returned HTTP 403.
limits: Snippet from a web search summary; do not quote effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: partial independent support with a moderator, unverified.

source: Gilhooly (2016) Incubation and intuition in creative problem solving, Segal (2004) description
finding: Segal 2004 used a spatial insight problem (parallelogram on a square). A break after impasse helped; break length (4 vs 12 min) and demand (crossword vs newspapers) did not matter. Gilhooly gives no N or statistics.
numbers: Return to task for up to 6 more minutes after the break. Result stated only in words. Weisberg is cited for the Intermittent Work account and for showing that the Coleridge, Mozart and Kekule stories are false; no Bowden null result is reported.
quote: Results indicated significant benefits for incubation break v. no break, but no effects for length of break or for the demandingness
limits: Second-hand; Gilhooly is an advocate. Sample sizes still unknown.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open (N and effect sizes); Gap 8 Bowden stays open. Segal's no-demand-effect finding is the odd one out.

source: Steindorf, Rummel and Boywitt (2021) Thinking about unconscious thought (Frontiers in Psychology, doi 10.3389/fpsyg.2021.545928)
finding: Three experiments on an apartment-evaluation decision task. Unconscious thought effect present in the first two only; probing thoughts during the filler removed the benefit. Not an insight task.
numbers: N = 822 across three experiments. Per-experiment statistics not extracted.
limits: Decision task, not insight; abstract and introduction read, not the full results.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: later unconscious-thought work is decision-based and mixed, so it cannot settle insight incubation. No insight-task replication found.

source: Lowe 2025 sleep-stage replication of Lacaux 2021, as reported in a news summary
finding: Preregistered conceptual replication found N2, not N1, as the stage linked to insight. Same pattern as already recorded in evidence_b and the critique.
numbers: Group sizes 18 wake, 22 N1, 28 N2 (matches critique). Spectral slope also predicted insight beyond stage.
limits: Press summary only here; the paper was opened in an earlier step. Non-randomised stage groups.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 stays open. No larger or randomised stage test was found in this run.

source: Fascendini, McGregor, Gupta and Griffiths (2026) The Riddle Riddle
finding: LLMs over-apply inventive reasoning: far better on genuine riddles than on riddle-like problems with literal answers. Humans show the reverse.
numbers: Nine LLMs (including GPT-5.4, Claude-opus-4-6, Gemini 3.1 Pro), 100 humans. LLMs 84.9% on genuine riddles vs 50.7% on riddle riddles; humans 50.5% vs 80.5%. 90.8% of LLM errors on riddle riddles were inventive overreach; 57.6% of human errors on genuine riddles were literal overreach. No thinking mode used.
limits: Non-thinking modes; no verification step tested; LLM judge agreement 0.90 to 0.93.
agent_relevance: A scaffold insight-style step should be gated: forcing a reframe on problems that need a literal answer hurts. Supports a verify state that checks the literal reading.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) NazoNazo benchmark (arXiv 2509.14704), verification-failure framing
finding: Search summary repeats that models often produce the right candidate and then fail to commit. No test found that moves verification to code or an independent sample at equal tokens.
numbers: Figures already recorded in c08, c09 (verification failures 5 to 39%).
limits: Only a summary page seen this step.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open: no equal-token verifier study found on insight riddles.

source: Bulut (2026) restart dose-response and intermediate solvability, same paper
finding: Many problems are neither solved nor unsolvable: about a third of ambiguous intermediate states stay at success 0.3 to 0.6 after eight attempts. Restarts help a compute-starved model and not a capability-limited one.
numbers: Ministral-3 3B: 0% to 79% of unsolved problems solved as restart budget grew; Gemma-4 E4B flat.
agent_relevance: Whether a retry helps depends on the model's regime. An agent should cap retries and test whether more samples change anything.
